recipes.name: Spiced Sweet Roasted Red Pepper Hummus

steps.text: In an electric blender or food processor, purée garbanzo beans, red peppers, lemon juice, tahini, garlic, cumin, cayenne, and salt. Use long pulses to process until mixture is fairly smooth and slightly fluffy, scraping down the sides in between pulses. Transfer to a serving bowl and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or up to 3 days.
Return to room temperature and sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Spiced Sweet Roasted Red Pepper Hummus
raw_recipe.description: This red pepper hummus is both spicy and sweet, and it's so easy to make — just pop everything into the food processor, pulse, and chill!

video.description: See how to make a roasted red pepper hummus that's both spicy and just a little sweet. This tasty appetizer is so quick and easy to make.

review.reviewBody: Mmmmmm! This recipe is excellent. I roasted my own peppers (To do this, place pepper directly on the burner over a medium flame until skin is blackened on all sides, toss in ice water, remove skin, and voila! roasted red pepper) Soooo good! and much cheaper than store bought.

This was wonderful! I added some chopped roasted garlic instead of minced. Put it all into my Nutri Bullet. I reserved some of the garbanzo bean juice from the can. I was worried that it might be a little too thick for the bullet. So I added some juice towards the end. It made creamier and it was fantastic!

This was really good. I roasted a red pepper and removed the skin. I also added 3 cloves of garlic because i like it spicy. I made my own tahini with sesame seeds and olive oil. I also added 1/2 teaspoon of sesame oil.I doubled the cumin and cayenne pepper. added just a teaspoon of sugar. I added some olive oil and a couple of tablespoons of the reserved juice from the beans. It was better than store bought for sure and it makes much more too. After it sits in the frig overnight it is the perfect texture.

I make a double batch of this regularly. When doubling it, I use three garlic cloves, and use heaping teaspoons of both the cayenne and cumin. I also add a bit of olive oil and let the food processor run for about five minutes. Lastly I use equal parts of lemon juice and tahini (1/4 cup each when making a double batch). I usually add some of the water from the roasted red pepper jar until I get the consistency I prefer.

If you use chickpeas that have been dried instead of canned, I think it tastes even better. When you do that you need to double the salt and also use additional water to get the consistency the way you like it. After you make it and it sits for a while, it tends to get thicker, so I make it a little on the runny side.

This is a great recipe and you can add or subtract depending on your palate. I always more garlic and tahini because we're addicted to both! I could roast my own peppers but I really like Mezzetta bottled roasted red peppers-mild. Instead of parsley, I use cilantro because we like the flavor and use it with many dishes. I've made this several times already. No more store-bought hummus for us! Thanks so much for this recipe!

Tastes great. Tahini is hard to find, especially in the middle of the night when ethnic markets are closed and 24-hour grocery stores don't generally carry it (generally when I would crave something like this).. As a substitute for tahini I blended 1/2 tablespoon of toasted sesame seeds in a food processor for ~15seconds, and added a tablespoon of natural peanut butter (i used Adams 100% natural peanut butter), and a drizzle of sesame seed oil if you can find it (i found all 3 of these ingredients at wal-mart), then I put in the rest of the ingredients listed on the recipe and processed. Turned out awesome. Roasting your own peppers is also better, just roast directly over stove top flame or grill until evenly charred all over. Mm mm delicious!

This turned out so good! It was way better then store bought and cheaper!!! I went to the store to buy tahini (i have never bought or used before) and the stuff is expensive and only comes in fairly large amounts...so i decided to make my own since all it is is sesame seed paste. To make, slow cook sesame seeds for 15min @ 300. make sure the don't brown. I did 1/4 cup seeds. the ratio is 1 part oil to 4 parts seeds. Place seeds in food processor with 1/2 the oil and pulse until mixed then add the rest of oil and chop/pulse until it forms a paste. When I first mixed all my ingredients together I though the tahini overpowered the recipe but once it chilled for about an hour it was PERFECT!!! I will make this all the time!!

Delicious! I made my own tahini, roasted my own peppers, (fabulous quick video if you search this site for "roasted red peppers"), and Instant Pot cooked dry garbanzos rather than canned. Skipped the olive oil to save calories. Flavor and texture is outstanding! This recipe is definitely a keeper. ??

Made this for my family's Pre-Christmas party. My mom loves it!! To ensure the hummus has a smoother consistency, I always pop the chickpeas off their skin. I used 1 can of chickpeas and 1 can of Butter beans. I didn't have cayenne pepper so I used smoked paprika powder. I also used two large freshly roasted red peppers (baked 230degrees 30mins) skinned. Even the caramelised juice from the peppers were added into the processor for extra flavour. Fresh lemon juice AND lemon peel all added into the processor too! 
Initially the hummus was too hot for liking so I added more Tahini. I also used sesame oil and extra virgin olive oil to make it smoother. if some water reserved from the can of beans are added, the hummus would have been even smoother amd softer!

mmmmm GOOD! I did add a tsp of Olive Oil. While rinsing the beans, you may want to take the time to gently rub them between your hands to remove the "skins" on them. It (IMO) makes a big difference in the flavor and texture.

Loved the hummus with the roasted red peppers! I cut back a bit on the cayenne pepper but the lemon juice really hit the spot! To make the tahini from scratch I put 1 cup olive oil to 1 cup roasted sesame seeds (they were in bulk at the store), blend that, then put in the chick peas (with the liquid), 2 garlic cloves not minced, and the rest... made TONS and cut up veggies which was a huge hit! Defintely make this again!!
Made as written, would have liked more zing.
I used cilantro instead of parsley, cuz I love cilantro and I don't care for parsley much.
Added 1tsp of olive oil. Great flavour.

I've made this recipe at least a half dozen times. It's my very favorite hummus recipe. I love to have it with veggies for a snack or as part of a meal. I don't always have fresh basil on hand, but when available, it really adds a lot. Excellent recipe!
Absolutely delicious….make it every NYE.

AMAZEZEBALLS! My hubby eats w/lunch everyday, so I increased recipe to 32 servings. 
Our personal preference: I add an extra can of beans, reduce the cumin & cayenne (to taste) and increase tahini to 1/3-1/2C. 
It lasts him about a week...SO much cheaper than store bought!

This was delicious! I'd never made hummus before and thought I'd give it try. This recipe was perfect and I followed it with 3 exceptions. 1) I roasted my own red bell peppers; 2) I added an additional clove of garlic; and 3) I skipped the parsley (not my thing).
A little too spicy for the kids, so I would suggest less cayenne. It was also too dry, so I added some olive oil. Really good and so easy!
Really easy and very tasty. Served it with raw veg
